summary: Aircraft Warning Service ground cabin on Caliente Mountain (San Luis Obispo County), built 1943; collapsed by 2013 and listed as removed; access restricted.

facts.design: Ground cabin with an observation cupola, built for Aircraft Warning Service use
facts.agency: United States Army Ground Observer Corps
facts.status_note: Cabin collapsed by 2013; the register lists the structure as removed, with collapsed remains

access.note: A February 2013 blog post says ranchers and oil-company security blocked the writer's attempt on the south side of the peak, a climb he called off-limits; no public route is described

events.note: District Ranger E. M. Lyda planned to investigate a lookout on Caliente peak (Santa Maria Times, October 1935, as quoted by Forest Lookouts)
Built for Aircraft Warning Service use; ground cabin with observation cupola
Cabin found fully collapsed, per a February 2013 blog post; the blogger estimates it fell before early May 2012 from summit entries
Registered December 20, 2019 as US 1861, CA 56, nominated by Brad Eells

notes_for_editor: Built 1943 rests on the register alone (plus its 1943 photo caption); the 1935 proposal is a single newspaper report quoted by Forest Lookouts. The collapse date is an estimate: the 2013 blog post says 'last year' for when the cabin likely fell, so it reads as before early May 2012 and is flagged as an estimate. The blog calls the cabin a WWII lookout, which fits the 1943 AWS date. No source describes staffing at this site specifically, so the story describes the AWS volunteer system only. No source describes the site after the 2013 visit. Access is restricted per the 2013 blog (ranch and oil-company land); the blog also describes reaching the summit by another route, which the story deliberately omits. The register's elevation 5,109 ft (1,557 m) is the site figure; Wikipedia gives the summit as 5,106 ft (1,556 m).
